note: Owner-authored entity synopses, layered onto public/data/entity-hovers.json. Keyed by the permanent qe- entity id, never by display name, alias or slug.
why: The published hovers were generated by scripts/extract-entity-hovers.mjs from a handoff folder of JSONL audit files that no longer exists on this machine, so the generator cannot be re-run and a synopsis cannot be added at its source. It would be the wrong place regardless: a ruling written into a derived artifact is erased the next time its audit runs. This file is the owner layer, and scripts/apply-entity-synopses.mjs applies it on top.
wording: A synopsis says who or what the entity IS, for a reader hovering the term in a drop. It states the identity and the reason the archive holds it, and it does not adopt Q's framing or assert a contested claim as fact. The generated line it replaces said only 'X is categorized in this archive as a person. It appears N times across M posts.', which tells a reader nothing they could not already see.

synopses.provenance: Owner ruling on #1929: 'this is Nellie Ohr (Bruce Ohr's Wife) ... lets make a little synopsis about who she is so if we hover over the term readers know.'
synopses.synopsis: Nellie Ohr is a Russia researcher who worked as a contractor for the private research firm Fusion GPS during 2016, the year it commissioned the Steele dossier. She is married to Bruce Ohr, then a senior official at the US Department of Justice. Their overlap — a DOJ official whose wife worked for the firm behind the dossier — made both of them a focus of congressional inquiries into the origins of the FBI's Russia investigation. Q writes her as the initials NO, almost always paired with her husband's BO.
synopses.note: Q's pairing of the two sets of initials is what fixes the reference; the synopsis records the relationship without adopting any claim the drops make about it.
